account:
It is day 1, about 09:26, and I am in my office after a quiet morning. I read the appointment books early and have kept office hours. Next is the mill grain inspection at ten, lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen, tea with my neighbour at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, and the great hall at eighteen.

The unusual business is the innkeeper's specially arranged evening meeting, described only as a community hospitality matter. The innkeeper asked me to bring only myself, said no preparation was needed, and obtained the secretary's promise to remind and escort me. It is confirmed in the updated appointment book. Separately, last evening I heard the baker asking the builder how many loaves had reached the hall, where freight was, and about unresolved grain funding. This morning my neighbour said the baker, freight, and innkeeper had been coordinating a bread order, but did not know its outcome. These arrangements may be connected with the hospitality meeting—perhaps refreshments for a gathering—but I have not been told their purpose and cannot confirm that connection.

The baker briefly appeared near the office this morning. I greeted them, but my greeting was not recorded as heard by the baker, and I received no reply. My neighbour asked about the bread order too; I heard no answer. The neighbour's visit was otherwise friendly, and tea at three remains arranged.

Town accounts remain unresolved. Yesterday the treasury contained 128 emeralds, but no ledger or supporting financial records were available. The secretary has retained a request for records; we still do not know their custodian. No new correspondence had been handed to the secretary this morning. I have asked that incoming council letters be received here for my thirteen-o'clock session. I have no evidence of a crisis or wrongdoing; the main uncertainty is the bread arrangements and the purpose of tonight's hospitality meeting.
